UDR.thesis_one_line: A large, diversified apartment landlord buying back its own historically cheap stock, even though rent growth has stalled and Southern-market supply still weighs on results.
kill_criteria: Same-store NOI growth negative for two consecutive quarters (FY26 guide is barely positive at +0.625% midpoint).
Consolidated Net Debt-to-EBITDAre (adjusted) rises above 6.0x (from 5.6x now).
FFO-as-Adjusted per-share guidance is cut (not just plain FFO) at either of the next two quarterly updates.
Southeast or Southwest same-store NOI decline exceeds -4% YoY in any quarter (supply absorption failing, not just slowing).
Share buyback program paused or reduced to a token level for two consecutive quarters (loss of the primary capital-return signal underpinning the thesis).
Added by RA14: FFO-as-Adjusted guide midpoint falls below $2.50 (now $2.53), or the next unsecured refinancing prices above 6.25% (current average coupon 3.31%)
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 GAAP diluted EPS rose +91% YoY ($0.21 vs $0.11) almost entirely on a $35.7M gain on sale of real estate; FFO per share actually fell -1.6% YoY ($0.60 vs $0.61) and FFO-as-Adjusted was flat ($0.64 vs $0.64).

1H26 operating cash flow fell -3.8% YoY ($390.9M vs $406.5M) even as GAAP net income more than doubled ($276.6M vs $114.4M) -- an earnings-quality gap driven by gains on property sales ($193.1M in 1H26 vs $47.9M in 1H25).

The July 27, 2026 release headlined 'raises full-year guidance' but the plain FFO/share guidance midpoint was actually cut $0.02 (to $2.51 from $2.53); only FFO-as-Adjusted and Net Income guidance rose.

FY2026 guided FFO-as-Adjusted per share midpoint ($2.53) is essentially flat versus FY2025's actual ($2.54); FFOA/share has been range-bound $0.61-$0.65 for eight consecutive quarters -- no per-share growth in two years, despite V1's +22%/yr base case.

Same-store NOI is contracting in the Southeast (-2.0% YoY Q2'26) and Southwest (-2.2% YoY Q2'26), 23% of the same-store portfolio, due to new supply; full-year 2026 same-store NOI guidance is barely positive (+0.625% midpoint).
Consolidated Net Debt-to-EBITDAre (adjusted) is 5.6x, up from 5.5x a year ago, on the higher side of the multifamily REIT peer range.
Two close peers, AvalonBay and Equity Residential, announced an all-stock merger in 2026 and suspended their own FFO guidance, reshaping UDR's competitive/comp set.
FY2025 actual FFO ($2.43) missed the bottom of the company's own final FY2025 guidance range ($2.44-$2.46) by one cent.

On AFFO per share ($2.24: FFOA $2.53 less about $0.29 recurring capex) the yield is 6.6% and the $1.74 dividend is 78% of AFFO; the 3.31% average coupon on $5.83B of debt re-prices toward about 5.8% as it matures, a drag of about $0.07 per share a year for each $1B refinanced.
data_conflicts: V1's reverse-DCF used TTM capex of $7.76M (0.45% of revenue) for UDR; the Q2 2026 10-Q cash-flow statement shows $104.2M of 'capital expenditures and other major improvements' plus $53.0M of development capex for just 1H26 (~$314M annualized, ~18% of revenue) -- roughly 20-40x the D3 figure feeding V1. This understates V1's FCFF and biases the reverse-DCF's implied growth (-5.2%) too far negative, making the stock look more underpriced-for-growth than a corrected calculation would show.

V1's peer_median (44.6x) for UDR's P/FFO comparison is NTM GAAP P/E of peers (CPT, ESS, MAA, and an unrecognised 'VMRK' ticker), not true P/FFO -- flagged as unreliable by V1 itself; true peer P/FFO multiples were not independently reconstructed within the time box.

V1's share count (330.3M) omits 22.2M OP/DownREIT units and 2.8M Series E shares as converted (economic count 346.3M, market cap $11.72B); V1's WACC of 6.54% used a 3.3% debt cost; V1's base scenario used year-3 FFO/share of $2.33 and a 24.1x exit multiple from peers' GAAP P/E (UDR trades at 13.4x FFOA, apartment peers 14.6-16.1x), so its +21.9% a year base return is not usable.
UDR.confidence_in_thesis: medium -- the statistical cheapness vs. own history and the real, verified buyback are solid evidence, but near-term FFO growth is flat (guided and delivered), leverage has crept up, and V1's implied-growth math needed a material correction, so conviction is capped at a small/half-weight position rather than full INCLUDE.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I agree UDR is statistically cheap versus its own 15-year P/FFO history, but V1's capex input was understated by roughly 20-40x (verified against the 10-Q cash-flow statement), which overstates how negative the reverse-DCF's implied growth looks and inflates V1's 0.874 score; correcting it would still show the stock as reasonably priced but far less dramatically so. V1 also does not see that FY2026 guided FFOA is flat YoY and that leverage has risen, both of which argue for a smaller position than V1's score alone implies -- hence INCLUDE-SMALL, not full INCLUDE. RESTATED 6 Oct 2026 (RA14): on AFFO per share ($2.24 for 2026) with a 9.2% cost of equity (5.17% Treasury + 0.807 x 5.0%) the price implies +1.7% growth for ten years (+0.2% at 8.5%, +3.4% at 10.0%), not -5.2%, versus an evidence-based +2% to +3% (FFOA $2.57 / $2.63 / $2.71 in 2027-29 given a flat two-year record, same-store NOI guide 0-1.25% and refinancing drag); the base path returns 9.7% against 9.2% and is worth about $36.7 (+8%). UDR trades about 15% below apartment peers on FFOA (13.4x vs 14.6-16.1x), so the 'cheap' wording becomes 'fair'. V1's scenario returns (-7.4% / +21.9% / +57.4%) are replaced by -1.6% / +8.3% / +15.2% (probability-weighted +7.0%).

UDR.scenario_basis: 3-year (to Sep 2029) annualised from $33.84, own arithmetic on FFO as Adjusted per share (guide midpoint $2.53 for 2026): bear -3% / -3% / -1.7% a year (same-store NOI negative, refinancing drag), base +1.5% / +2.5% / +3.0%, bull +4% / +5.5% / +6%; trailing FFOA at Sep 2029 $2.35 / $2.69 / $2.90; exit P/FFOA 11.5x / 14.0x / 16.0x (today 13.4x; apartment-REIT peers 14.6-16.1x); dividends $1.74 a year ($5.25 over three years). Weights 30/45/25 give +7.0%. Replaces V1 (-7.4% / +21.9% / +57.4%), whose base used FFO/share $2.33 and a 24.1x exit multiple taken from peers' GAAP P/E.

PSA.thesis_one_line: The largest self-storage landlord just closed a huge stock-funded acquisition, but its existing storage units are still losing rent and cash flow per share.
kill_criteria: Same-store NOI growth remains negative for full-year 2026 as reported (confirming the current -1.15%-midpoint guidance rather than a further raise into positive territory).

NSA merger fails to show positive Core FFO accretion in the first full reported quarter of combination (Q3 or Q4 2026 reported Core FFO per share, pro forma for the enlarged share count, below what a standalone-PSA trajectory would have produced).
Net Debt-and-Preferred-Equity to EBITDA rises above 5.0x (from 4.2x now).
Same-store realized annual rent per occupied square foot declines for four consecutive quarters (currently two: Q1'26 and Q2'26).
The pending Public Storage Canada acquisition fails to close, or closes on materially worse terms, by year-end 2026.
key_adverse_facts: Same-store revenue and NOI are declining: Q2 2026 same-store revenue -0.6% YoY, same-store NOI -2.2% YoY (1H26: -0.3%/-1.0%); realized annual rent per occupied square foot fell for a second straight quarter (-0.8% Q2 YoY).

Core FFO per share fell -2.6% YoY in Q2 2026 ($4.17 vs $4.28) and has declined every quarter since peaking at $4.31 in Q3 2025, even as GAAP diluted EPS rose +44.9% YoY ($2.55 vs $1.76) -- the GAAP gain is almost entirely a foreign-currency swing on Euro-denominated debt (+$17.2M vs -$146.1M a year earlier); operating income itself fell -6.7% YoY in Q2.

FY2026 guidance, even after being raised in July, still calls for full-year same-store NOI to decline (-2.0% to -0.3%, midpoint -1.15%) and full-year Core FFO per share ($16.75-$17.05, midpoint $16.90) essentially flat versus FY2025's actual $16.97 -- not the +18%/yr V1 base case.

PSA closed the ~$10.5B all-stock acquisition of National Storage Affiliates on July 22, 2026 (~11.2M new shares issued) and has a second, separate ~$1.2B pending acquisition of Public Storage Canada expected to close Q3 2026, funded by $5.9B of 2026 debt and $6.0B of equity/OP-unit issuance YTD; management's own Q2 guidance attributes only $0.02/share of the current-year raise to financing accretion -- minimal proven M&A benefit so far, with expected full accretion ($0.35-0.50/share) not due until synergies stabilize over 3-4 years.

Three shareholder lawsuits were filed against NSA/Public Storage over the merger seeking injunctive relief and additional disclosures (routine 'disclosure' litigation typical of large stock M&A; company states claims lack merit and supplemented disclosures) -- a real but low-severity legal overhang.

G&A expense rose +72.5% YoY in Q2 2026 ($44.4M vs $25.7M), driven by NSA/PS Canada transaction and integration costs, a corporate-transformation restructuring program, and CEO-transition costs, which Core FFO excludes.

A sitting board member (Tamara Hughes Gustavson) and her family hold a related-party equity interest in, and license the Public Storage brand to, PS Canada -- the entity Public Storage is separately acquiring for ~$1.2B.
data_conflicts: V1's reverse-DCF proxied PSA's missing TTM capex with full trailing D&A ($1.164B, 23.8% of revenue) because D3's capex_ttm field was null. The Q2 2026 10-Q cash-flow statement shows actual maintenance-type capex (maintain + enhancements + energy) of only ~$269M annualized (~5.5% of revenue) -- about a quarter of what V1 assumed. This overstates V1's capex drag, which mechanically inflates the reverse-DCF's implied 10-year growth rate (25.3%); correcting it would likely raise V1's composite score, not lower it, since the 'achievable minus implied growth' penalty is the main reason V1 says only 'fair'.

V1's valuation inputs (diluted_shares = 176,512,000; market_cap = $50.83B) are pre-merger figures (Q2 2026 weighted-average shares, quarter ended June 30, 2026) that do not reflect the ~11.2 million new PSA common shares (plus ~4.1 million OP units and new preferred series) issued July 22, 2026 to close the National Storage Affiliates acquisition, nor NSA's added assets, earnings, or assumed/JV debt -- even though the merger had already closed two months before the 2026-09-25 cutoff. V1's entire per-share valuation snapshot for PSA is therefore stale.

V1's peer_median (28.1x) is EXR's NTM GAAP P/E (peer_n=2, i.e. EXR vs PSA itself), not a true P/FFO peer comparison -- flagged as unreliable by V1 itself; true peer P/FFO multiples for EXR/CUBE were not independently reconstructed within the time box.
PSA.confidence_in_thesis: medium -- the evidence of a deteriorating same-store business and a stale, doubly-flawed valuation model (capex proxy plus pre-merger share count) is clear and well-sourced, so confidence is high that this is not yet a full-conviction buy; confidence in the eventual NSA-integration outcome itself is genuinely low given how recently the deal closed.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's 'fair' score is itself built on two stacked errors that point in different directions -- an overstated capex proxy (which understates V1's score) and a pre-merger share count/business snapshot (which makes the whole calculation moot post-NSA) -- so I cannot simply endorse or correct V1's number. Weighing the primary-sourced evidence of a shrinking same-store business and unproven merger integration more heavily than either version of the stale model, I land on WATCH, which is more cautious than V1's already-lukewarm 'fair' label, not less.
